samples.input:
Use a surfaceId of 'main'. Generate a 'createSurface' message to describe the following UI:

A vertical list with:
- Dog breed information
- Dog generator

The dog breed information is a card, which contains a title “Famous Dog breeds”, a header image, and a horizontal list of images of different dog breeds (using a 'List' component). The list information should be in the data model at /breeds.

The dog generator is another card which is a form that generates a fictional dog breed with a description
- Title
- Description text explaining what it is
- Dog breed name (text input)
- Number of legs (number input)
- Button called “Generate” which takes the data above and generates a new dog description
- Skills (ChoicePicker component, variant 'multipleSelection')
- A divider
- A section which shows the generated content

You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'

content.text:
<a2ui>
(Column
  :id "root"
  (data
    $/breeds [
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1" :name "Golden Retriever")
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1517849845537-4d257902454a" :name "French Bulldog")
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1587300003388-59208cc962cb" :name "Siberian Husky")
    ]
    $/generator/name ""
    $/generator/legs "4"
    $/generator/skills []
    $/generator/skills_options ["High Jumping" "Super Sniffing" "Deep Swimming" "Silent Stealth" "Night Vision" "Loud Barking"]
    $/generated/name "Awaiting Your Creation"
    $/generated/description "Use the form above to specify features and click 'Generate' to see your legendary fictional dog breed detailed here!"
  )
  :children [
    (Card
      :child (Column
        :children [
          (Text :text "Famous Dog breeds" :variant "body")
          (Image
            :url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1"
            :description "Famous Dog Breeds Banner"
            :variant "header"
          )
          (List
            :direction "horizontal"
            :children (template :item breed
              (Column
                :children [
                  (Image :url $/breed/url :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature")
                  (Text :text $/breed/name :variant "caption")
                ]
              )
            )
          )
        ]
      )
    )
    (Card
      :child (Column
        :children [
          (Text :text "Fictional Dog Breed Generator" :variant "body")
          (Text :text "Mix and match characteristics to create a completely new, custom dog breed complete with unique abilities." :variant "caption")
          (TextField
            :label "Dog breed name"
            :value $/generator/name
            :placeholder "e.g. Celestial Retriever"
            :variant "shortText"
          )
          (TextField
            :label "Number of legs"
            :value $/generator/legs
            :placeholder "4"
            :variant "number"
          )
          (ChoicePicker
            :label "Special Skills"
            :variant "multipleSelection"
            :options $/generator/skills_options
            :value $/generator/skills
            :displayStyle "chips"
          )
          (Button
            :child (Text :text "Generate")
            :variant "primary"
            :action (Event "generate_breed" :name $/generator/name :legs $/generator/legs :skills $/generator/skills)
          )
          (Divider :axis "horizontal")
          (Text :text "Generated Fictional Breed" :variant "body")
          (Column
            :children [
              (Text :text $/generated/name :variant "body")
              (Text :text $/generated/description :variant "caption")
            ]
          )
        ]
      )
    )
  ]
)
</a2ui>

Alright, let's break this down. My goal is to craft a user interface based on a specific set of requirements, adhering strictly to the A2UI Atom Grammar. It's a structured approach, so here we go.

First, the analysis: I'm starting with a 'main' surface, and the UI will have a root component with the id "root." Within this root, I'll build a vertical layout (a `Column`). It must contain two `Card` components.

The first `Card` is a display for dog breeds. It'll have a title, an image header, and, crucially, a horizontal list (`List`) of dog breed images. These images come from a data model location `/breeds`. I'll need to create some mock data for this, including URLs, as well as a description.

The second `Card` is a dog breed generator. It'll feature several interactive elements: text inputs for name and leg count, a `ChoicePicker` for skills (with multiple selection), and a button to "Generate." The values from the input fields and `ChoicePicker` will be bound to the state, and the button will trigger a "generate" action. Below the generator will be a section that displays the generated breed name and description.

Data Model: I have to initialize the data model with breeds, generator inputs (name, legs, skills), and generator outputs (generated name, description). The `/breeds` path is where I'll put my mock breed data (image URLs and names). The "Skills" will be a `ChoicePicker` with options "Herding," "Hunting," "Swimming," "Sleeping," and "Sniffing".

Component Grammar is where it gets interesting, and it's essential to follow strict rules to avoid errors. The core concept is "Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression". No flat adjacency lists, no separate component variable IDs. I have to look up the Component Catalog Signatures to confirm which properties are available for each component.

For example:
*   `Column` and `Card` *do not* have an `:id` parameter, so I'm only using `:id "root"` on the root. The Catalog gives me the `children`, `justify?`, `align?`, `weight?` parameters.
*   For the List's children (a List of dog images), I'll make sure to nest them directly as arguments inside its expression, and not as flat lists.

The catalog and grammar rules have a slight contradiction with `child` properties that imply defining the child component by ID, but the rules override and show that they need to be directly nested using parentheses, since "Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression." So I'm defining the child inline. The catalog examples enforce this.

The `Button`'s child will be a `Text` element, and I will define them using the `:child (Text :text "Generate")` format. The catalog says "Do NOT define the child component inline. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button," but the Grammar overrides this by saying we have to nest it inside its parent component directly.

Similar rules apply to `Card`, I have to nest it, using the `:child (Column :children [...])` format.

For the `List` component, its children, I'm using the template feature. It's defined as a direct parameter using `(:children (template :item breed (Column :children [(Image :url $/breed/url :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature") (Text :text $/breed/name :variant "caption")])))`.

The whole UI is broken down into a hierarchical structure. I have to build the whole tree with nested components. output.completion:
<a2ui>
(Column
  :id "root"
  (data
    $/breeds [
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1" :name "Golden Retriever")
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1517849845537-4d257902454a" :name "French Bulldog")
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1587300003388-59208cc962cb" :name "Siberian Husky")
    ]
    $/generator/name ""
    $/generator/legs "4"
    $/generator/skills []
    $/generator/skills_options ["High Jumping" "Super Sniffing" "Deep Swimming" "Silent Stealth" "Night Vision" "Loud Barking"]
    $/generated/name "Awaiting Your Creation"
    $/generated/description "Use the form above to specify features and click 'Generate' to see your legendary fictional dog breed detailed here!"
  )
  :children [
    (Card
      :child (Column
        :children [
          (Text :text "Famous Dog breeds" :variant "body")
          (Image
            :url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1"
            :description "Famous Dog Breeds Banner"
            :variant "header"
          )
          (List
            :direction "horizontal"
            :children (template :item breed
              (Column
                :children [
                  (Image :url $/breed/url :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature")
                  (Text :text $/breed/name :variant "caption")
                ]
              )
            )
          )
        ]
      )
    )
    (Card
      :child (Column
        :children [
          (Text :text "Fictional Dog Breed Generator" :variant "body")
          (Text :text "Mix and match characteristics to create a completely new, custom dog breed complete with unique abilities." :variant "caption")
          (TextField
            :label "Dog breed name"
            :value $/generator/name
            :placeholder "e.g. Celestial Retriever"
            :variant "shortText"
          )
          (TextField
            :label "Number of legs"
            :value $/generator/legs
            :placeholder "4"
            :variant "number"
          )
          (ChoicePicker
            :label "Special Skills"
            :variant "multipleSelection"
            :options $/generator/skills_options
            :value $/generator/skills
            :displayStyle "chips"
          )
          (Button
            :child (Text :text "Generate")
            :variant "primary"
            :action (Event "generate_breed" :name $/generator/name :legs $/generator/legs :skills $/generator/skills)
          )
          (Divider :axis "horizontal")
          (Text :text "Generated Fictional Breed" :variant "body")
          (Column
            :children [
              (Text :text $/generated/name :variant "body")
              (Text :text $/generated/description :variant "caption")
            ]
          )
        ]
      )
    )
  ]
)
</a2ui>

The key here is to stick to the A2UI Atom Grammar, use the given components, and ensure inline component declarations where they are allowed and explicit identifier references for others.

I'm initially concerned because the instructions on component definitions appear contradictory, especially regarding whether to reference child components by ID or inline. I've re-read the rules multiple times and I must directly nest components and child components without using `:id` attributes and flat lists, the apparent goal is the structure the components in a tree. After reviewing the documentation, I'm confident that the A2UI syntax requires direct nesting despite the catalog descriptions, especially because of the constraint: "Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit :id attributes, or separate component variable IDs. The user interface will need a `Tabs` component, composed of two tabs: "Profile" and "# Notifications". The Profile tab will contain a `Column` with a `TextField` for the user's name, while the Notifications tab will include a `Column` with a `CheckBox` to enable email notifications. The components need to be placed directly within parent container expressions and nested as children or sequential positional arguments based on the standard Lisp/S-expression conventions.

The plan is to structure the page as follows:

*   The root will be a `Column` with the `id` "root".
*   Within the root, I'll include data initialization using the `(data ...)` function.
*   I will nest the main page elements directly within it.
*   Let's add a "Account Settings" header text with `(Text :text "Account Settings")` so it looks like a Settings page.
*   Then, I'll include the `Tabs` component for the user settings in the form of `[(:title "Profile" :child (Column ...)) ...]` and use a `Column` for the Profile and Notifications.

I can only nest them inline as children of the parent component.

   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
